periodos.nombre: Iron Age I — Exodus Camp, Red Sea Crossing

descripcion_geo: Egyptian border town near the Red Sea, mentioned as one of the last camping points of Israel before the miraculous crossing of the waters during the departure of Egypt, and later as a destination for Jewish refugees after the fall of Jerusalem.
clima: Desert — extremely hot and dry, typical of the northeastern border region of Egypt.
recursos: Border position near the Red Sea
Geographical landmark of the exodus camp
importancia_estrategica: Migdol marks one of the last Israel camping spots during the Egypt exodus, just before the miraculous crossing of the Red Sea, strategically positioning the town between Migdol and the sea facing Baal-zephon; Centuries later, it reappears as a destination for Jewish refugees fleeing to Egypt after the fall of Jerusalem, closing an ironic geographical circle between the original departure of Egypt and the forced return of the descendants of those liberated.

otros_habitantes.descripcion: Village camping near Migdol on its exit route from Egypt, just before the miraculous crossing of the Red Sea.
Population of Judah that, after the destruction of Jerusalem, settles in Migdol among other Egyptian destinations, denounced by Jeremiah for adopting idolatrous practices in their new residence.

historias.titulo: Israel camps near Migdol before the Red Sea
historias.descripcion: YHWH instructs Moses to order Israel to camp between Migdol and the sea, facing Baal-zephon, an apparently vulnerable positioning that serves to lure Pharaoh's army into the trap of the later miraculous crossing.

historias.titulo: Migdol confirmed on the list of exodus camps
historias.descripcion: The book of Numbers confirms Migdol's position in the detailed list of Israel's campsites during his departure from Egypt, a record that systematically documents the entire pilgrimage route.

historias.titulo: Jeremiah denounces the idolatry of the Jews in Migdol
historias.descripcion: Jeremiah directs its prophetic denunciation specifically to the Jews residing in Migdol, Tahpanes, Memphis and other regions of Egypt, condemning their persistence in burning incense to the 'queen of heaven' despite the destruction of Jerusalem that such idolatry had caused.

personajes.descripcion: Direct the strategic positioning of Israel near Migdol before the miraculous crossing of the Red Sea, following divine instructions that appear to expose the people but in reality prepare the trap against the Egyptian army.

He denounces the persistent idolatry of the Jewish refugees in Migdol and other Egyptian cities, warning that their fate will be complete destruction for repeating the same sins that caused the fall of Jerusalem.

personajes.rol: Israel pursuers to the Red Sea
personajes.descripcion: He pursues Israel into the region of Migdol, deceived by the town's apparent vulnerable positioning, before being defeated at the miraculous crossing of the Red Sea.

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: Migdol ironically connects the beginning and a late moment in the history of Israel: a place of passage in the original liberation from Egyptian slavery under Moses, and centuries later, the destination of Jewish refugees who voluntarily return to Egypt fleeing the consequences of their own infidelity, closing a geographical circle that illustrates the contrast between the original providential liberation and the subsequent self-inflicted exile for the persistence in idolatry denounced by Jeremiah.
religiones_presentes: Egyptian polytheism (context of the exodus and subsequent refugees)

mitos.nombre: Seemingly vulnerable positioning as a divine trap in Migdol

judaismo.fuente_secundaria: Comentario rabínico tradicional sobre la sabiduría aparentemente contraintuitiva del posicionamiento divino de Israel antes del cruce del Mar Rojo
judaismo.descripcion: Jewish tradition observes that the divine command to position Israel in an apparently vulnerable place near Migdol, far from being a strategic error, constitutes precisely the mechanism by which YHWH draws the Egyptian army towards its definitive defeat, interpreting the episode as a paradigmatic example of how divine wisdom can manifest itself through strategies that from a human perspective would seem counterproductive.
judaismo.significado_teologico: Migdol's positioning teaches that divine wisdom frequently operates in ways that transcend and even contradict conventional human strategic logic.
